# Stutter Guard - SHA-256 checksums
#
# THE AUTHORITY FOR A DOWNLOAD IS THE .sha256 ATTACHED TO ITS RELEASE
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every release carries StutterGuard.exe.sha256, generated by the build job from the exact bytes it
# uploaded. Verify a download against that file:
#
#   certutil -hashfile StutterGuard.exe SHA256
#
# This file deliberately states no current hash. The build job runs .NET SDK 10.0.x on a GitHub runner,
# not in the maintainer's working copy, so its bytes are not ours to predict; and a hash recorded here
# goes stale the moment the next release is cut. That is exactly the failure this project has already
# had once - a published checksum that described a file nobody could download.
#
# ---- Hashes of released assets (historical record, complete as of v1.2.0) ----
01752CF8BCFAF8346516CFAC14DA0E1D2B468EBAACCC0923F0BAFBF39BC25B89  StutterGuard.exe  (v1.2.0)
#
# ---- The reproducible-build claim, stated as measured ----
#
# WHAT IS CLAIMED: two CLEAN publishes of one working tree, into two different directories, produce
# byte-identical output. Measured on 2026-11-15 and again on 2026-11-19, .NET SDK 10.0.402, win-x64, by
# `build.cmd --verify-repro`, which deletes every obj/ and bin/ between the two publishes so they cannot
# share results.
#
# WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED, and was measured to be false: that the SAME commit produces the same bytes at a
# different time. Commit b99fb44 (v1.4.0) was published cleanly twice on 2026-11-19 and gave two different
# files - 65,456,984 bytes / 4618F79B... at 05:56, and 65,456,986 bytes / D87906C1... at 06:11. Each pair
# was internally identical (the switch above passed on both runs, and again on a re-run), so the property
# is "a clean pair in one stretch of time is one file", not "a commit has a hash". The 2-byte size change
# is the same drift this file recorded before between two commits whose only difference was markdown, and
# it is still unexplained: no source path, timestamp or commit id was found to be embedded.
#
# THE CONSEQUENCE, which is why no absolute figure is stated here: a hash of your own build verifies the
# bytes in front of you and nothing else. The v1.4.0 release asset (65,462,615 bytes) was verified against
# the .sha256 attached to that release by downloading it, and that check passed; it is a third value again,
# because a different runner is a different build.
#
# WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: that a release's bytes equal a build of your own. They do not have to, and the
# absolute figure moves between working trees: cleaning and publishing commit c59b29b gave 65,446,991
# bytes (E36FE73D...), and commit 0b14fea - whose only difference was markdown and an SVG - gave
# 65,446,993 bytes (46C188BD...). That drift is not explained by anything this repository embeds, and
# stating no absolute number is the honest response to it rather than publishing a figure that looks
# authoritative and moves.
#
# WHAT IS ALSO MEASURED: an INCREMENTAL publish of the same source differs from a clean one
# (65,446,984 against 65,446,991 bytes). Reproducibility is a property of a clean build.
#
# Run it yourself before publishing anything:
#   build.cmd --verify-repro
